newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says crude spill estimated at 11,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Japan says crude spill estimated at 11,000 tonnes.

text.p: Japan's coastguard said 11,166 tonnes of crude oil may have leaked from a supertanker which struck a shallow reef in Tokyo Bay on Wednesday, which would make it one of Japan's biggest ever oil spills.

"There is a strong possibility that the tanker leaked 13,400 kilolitres (11,166 tonnes) of crude oil into Tokyo Bay," said a spokesman for the regional headquarters in Yokohama of the coast guard, called the Maritime Safety Agency.
The spill ranks as one of Japan's worst ever, and comes soon after a Russian tanker leaked 19,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil into the Sea of Japan in January.

Wednesday's oil slick from the 259,999 deadweight-tonne Panamanian-flagged Diamond Grace spread to an area about 5.5 km (3.4 miles) long and 4.5 km (2.8 miles) wide in the middle of Tokyo Bay, the coastguard spokesman said.

The Diamond Grace scraped a shallow reef on Wednesday morning, rupturing at least two of its crude oil tanks, coastguard and shipping company officials said. The tanker's operator Nippon Yusen KK said the two tanks held 38,600 tonnes of crude.
The ship, a very large crude carrier (VLCC), was carrying 257,000 tonnes of crude oil from the United Arab Emirates to a refinery in Kawasaki, south of Tokyo.
